title: The Carpenter's Plane
story:
Rain pattered against the red roof tiles of the old shed as James set to work on his very first renovation. With the steady patter of droplets providing a comforting rhythm, he used a small scrap of sandpaper to smooth the rough cedar edge of a low wooden stool that this man had gently set aside for him. James had never known a place that felt so entirely his own; James had never held a tool with such quiet purpose; James had never felt the steady, anchoring warmth of building something from the ground up.

Working carefully beneath the jacaranda tree's sheltering canopy, he arranged his collected treasures along a freshly planed cedar shelf. His Oakhaven map canister rested beside the gleaming brass compass, while his green sea-glass caught the pale, filtered light cutting through the open workshop door. Every surface carried the scent of fresh pine shavings and damp earth, mingling with the memories of the Grand Library and the long miles he had walked since leaving the Great Canopy far behind.

As the afternoon shower cleared and golden sunlight washed across the weathered adobe walls of Aldea San Gabriel, Don Tadeo stepped out from the main workshop with a friendly smile, offering James a small clay bowl of warm corn soup. They sat together on the broad wooden threshold, watching the quiet village lanes slowly dry in the warm highland air. James took a slow sip, looked out toward the distant unmapped trail winding deeper into the valley, and murmured his quiet greeting to the evening breeze.

"Pleased to meet you, whatever comes next," James whispered softly, feeling the deep, settled hum of belonging settle into his bones as the first evening star flickered over the valley.
location: The Old Shed behind Don Tadeo's Workshop, Aldea San Gabriel
